decisions.statement: Every file no property declares as bytes is judged.
A body a file property declares as bytes is let through.
A property naming its file is read from the file's own name.
That file is let through only where a page with the property sits in its folder.
A file of that name in another folder is judged.
A property naming no file is read from the section its files have.
A file that section names is let through only under a page type carrying that property.
Two properties sharing a section name are told apart by the page type in the name.
A body a folder property declares as bytes is let through.
That folder is read from the name the property states.
A file beneath that folder is let through only where a page with the property sits above it.
A file under a folder of that name elsewhere is judged.
A body an extension property declares as bytes is let through.
That extension is read from the name the property states.
A file closing that way is let through only where a page with the property sits in its folder.
A file closing that way in a folder beneath that page is judged.
A file with more than one NUL is reported at the first.
The report says how many NULs the file carries.
A NUL is counted in the bytes rather than in the decoded text.
A file a property declares as bytes is never opened.

definition: the check refusing a file with a raw NUL byte
